analysis.title: The Flow Show: Enter the Dragon
key_insights: BofA stays tactically risk-off until mid-November. It expects yields down (30-year Treasury toward 5%), stocks down and the US dollar down (DXY below 100) until a set of conditions is priced in.

The conditions that would end the risk-off view are: a Democratic midterm sweep fully priced in, the ECB or French government stopping the rout in French bonds, and an AI capex cut or extreme equity issuance announcement that marks a peak in AI hyperscaler debt spreads.

Near-term upside risk is the US announcing Russia/Ukraine/Iran peace deals that cut oil by $10-20/bbl. Near-term downside risk is hyperscaler bond spreads rising above 200bps, with investors deleveraging on shadow-banking credit event risk.

China stocks (CSI 300) are down 20% since June, led by tech (-41%). Yields are at a record low 1.6%, the currency is at a 4-year high, and property is still bleeding. BofA calls this a classic deflation combination with a consumer and investor buyer strike.
Global EPS risk is China export deflation: China exports are up 36% YoY and high-tech exports are up 63% YoY (about $147bn in September 2026).

Mid caps (MDY above $666), small caps (IJR above $137) and global financials (IXG above $125) are holding up. BofA reads the October risk-off as a tech de-rating in a tightening cycle, with NDX holding 28k.

Growth shows signs of breaking: MAGS is below $70 and TSM below $400, tech EPS is being revised down, and investors are the most overweight tech since Aug 2020 in the BofA October FMS. BRK is at new all-time highs, consistent with a value over growth rotation.

BofA takes a secular contrarian stance. It would add bonds, because US Treasury 10-year rolling returns are the worst in 100 years. It adds to 'peak yield' plays: small cap, REITs, utilities and consumer discretionary.
Capitulatory outflows from utility ($1.6bn) and consumer ($2.1bn) funds were each the 2nd largest on record, which BofA treats as supportive of the contrarian entry.

Three 2027 scenarios: AI bubble (AI as railroads, government backstop of AI, buy-the-dip ethos), Goldilocks breadth (consensus sees UST yields -40bps and 15% SPX EPS growth in 2027), and deflationary bust (credit tightening cuts the $1.2tn hyperscaler 2027 capex forecast).

BofA thinks consensus conviction in the bubble scenario (50% of FMS investors expect 'no landing') and the breadth scenario (40% 'soft landing') is too high. Fear of a 'hard landing' bust (6%) is too low.

Weekly flows: $55.6bn to stocks, $28.8bn to cash, $12.1bn to bonds, $2.6bn to gold, $0.2bn to crypto. Tech took in $18.8bn (largest since July 2026), China equities $17.0bn, Japan $6.0bn and Korea $5.8bn.

The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 7.2 from 7.4 (neutral), driven by weak global index breadth, bearish hedge fund positioning in oil and S&P 500 futures and wider junk spreads, partly offset by strong equity inflows.
The Breadth Rule shows net 30% of global markets oversold. The contrarian buy signal needs net 88%, which would take US, Taiwan and Brazil indices falling 5-10%.

YTD 2026 returns: oil +72.7%, US stocks +11.9%, global stocks +8.7%, US dollar +3.4%, cash +3.0%, HY -0.9%, IG -2.2%, government bonds -3.0%, gold -6.9%, bitcoin -7.1%. Korea equities lead at +66.4% and Taiwan is +62.6%.

tension_points.theme: 2027 AI bubble vs breadth vs bust
tension_points.bull_case: AI behaves like the railroads, with an unprecedented US government backstop and a structural buy-the-dip ethos. Or breadth broadens under Goldilocks, with consensus at 15% SPX EPS growth and a 40bps drop in UST yields in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Railroads had three 30-50% drawdowns during the late-1800s bull. Bonds end booms and credit tightening could cut the $1.2tn hyperscaler 2027 capex forecast. No AI boom means no boom, unless oil falls $30, yields fall 100-150bps and China stimulates.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler bond spreads surging above 200bps, or an AI capex cut or extreme equity issuance announcement.

tension_points.bull_case: Peace deals for Russia/Ukraine/Iran could cut oil by $10-20/bbl, and mid caps, small caps and financials are holding up.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech de-rating with EPS downward revisions, French bond rout, midterm Democratic sweep risk and hyperscaler credit spreads.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic midterm sweep fully priced in, the ECB or French government stopping the French bond rout, or an AI capex cut marking a peak in hyperscaler spreads.
